board_content.text: The conjugate-root theorem applies to real coefficients only.

segments_english.text: Here is the complete quadratic-roots toolkit for the whole subtopic on one board.
The formula: x equals minus b plus or minus root D, over two a, where D is b squared minus four a c.
For real coefficients, the discriminant forecasts the roots: positive means two distinct real, zero means one repeated real, negative means a complex-conjugate pair.
When D is negative, the roots are minus b plus or minus i root of four a c minus b squared, all over two a.
Vieta's relations: the sum of the roots is minus b over a, and the product is c over a.

To build a quadratic from roots, use x squared minus the sum times x plus the product. And for a real quadratic from a complex root p plus i q, it's x squared minus two p x plus p squared plus q squared.

The square root of a complex number: root of a plus i b is plus or minus x plus i y, where x squared is the modulus plus a over two, y squared is the modulus minus a over two, and the sign of the product x y matches the sign of b.
And the boundary line to never forget: the conjugate-root theorem applies to real coefficients only.

segments_hinglish.text: Ye raha poore subtopic ka complete quadratic-roots toolkit ek board par.
Formula: x equals minus b plus or minus root D, over two a, jahan D hai b squared minus four a c.
Real coefficients ke liye, discriminant roots forecast karta hai: positive matlab do distinct real, zero matlab ek repeated real, negative matlab ek complex-conjugate pair.
Jab D negative hai, roots hain minus b plus or minus i root of four a c minus b squared, poora over two a.
Vieta's relations: roots ka sum hai minus b over a, aur product hai c over a.
Roots se quadratic banane ke liye x squared minus sum times x plus product. Aur complex root p plus i q se real quadratic ke liye, wo hai x squared minus two p x plus p squared plus q squared.

Complex number ka square root: root of a plus i b hai plus or minus x plus i y, jahan x squared hai modulus plus a over two, y squared hai modulus minus a over two, aur product x y ka sign b ke sign se match karta hai.
Aur wo boundary line jo kabhi mat bhoolo: conjugate-root theorem sirf real coefficients par apply hota hai.
